glance: 205 km to Kushtia by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
kangal-harinath-museum.desc: Kangal Harinath Majumdar ran Gram Barta Prokashika from Kumarkhali in the 1860s, one of the first newspapers to write about the lives of peasants and the abuses of indigo planters and zamindars. He also wrote Baul songs and was close to Lalon's circle. The memorial museum, a branch of the Bangladesh National Museum, opened to visitors in 2017 and keeps his memory alive in the town. His old MN Press, among the oldest printing presses in the country, is in Kumarkhali too.
blocks: How to get there
Take a bus or CNG from Kushtia town to Kumarkhali (about 30–40 minutes), then a rickshaw.
Good to know
Combine with Shilaidaha Kuthibari and Mir Mosharraf Hossain's home, both in Kumarkhali upazila. Like most national museum branches, it is likely closed on a weekly holiday, so check before going.

kumarkhali-weaving.desc: Kumarkhali has long been a centre of handloom weaving in the Kushtia region. In weavers' homes you can watch cotton thread wound, dyed and woven into checked lungis, gamchas and bedcovers. The town also has a historic trading past on the Gorai river. Buying directly supports a craft facing competition from power looms.
blocks: Good to know
Ask in Kumarkhali bazar for weaving neighbourhoods; mornings are busiest.

glance: Kulfi sellers around Kushtia town, mostly in the afternoon
kushtia-kulfi-malai.desc: Ask a Bangladeshi about kulfi and many will say Kushtia. Local kulfi families boil cow's milk with sugar and cardamom in big iron pans over clay stoves for ten to twelve hours until it turns into thick malai. It is set into kulfi overnight and sold by the next afternoon. Makers say the local milk and water are part of the taste, which is why it is never quite the same elsewhere.
blocks: Good to know
Buy from a seller who made it that morning; it is meant to be eaten the same day.

glance: 205 km to Kushtia by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
gorai-railway-bridge.desc: Work on the Gorai Railway Bridge began in 1865, when the line from Kushtia was being extended east towards Goalundo. It is described as the first major railway bridge in present-day Bangladesh. The iron spans over the Gorai, with sandbanks below in the dry season, make a quiet spot for an evening walk along the riverbank. Trains still cross it, so the bridge itself is not for walking.
blocks: How to get there
From Kushtia town take an easy-bike east towards the Gorai riverbank by the rail line.
Good to know
View it from the bank; do not walk on the bridge, as it is a live railway line.

glance: 205 km to Kushtia by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
autumn (Aug–Sep), late autumn (Oct–Nov), winter (Dec–Jan) and spring (Feb–Mar)
lalon-akhra-cheuria.desc: Lalon Shah, the 19th-century mystic poet whose songs question caste and religious division, lived and died at Cheuria on the edge of Kushtia town. His domed white shrine and the akhra around it are a place of pilgrimage for Bauls and fakirs. On most evenings singers sit with ektara and dotara and perform his songs. A museum and academy on the grounds tell his story.
blocks: How to get there
A rickshaw or auto from Kushtia town or railway station, about 10–15 minutes.
Good to know
Sit and listen respectfully; offer a small donation if you record singers. Remove shoes near the shrine.

glance: 205 km to Kushtia by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
jagati-railway-station.desc: On 15 November 1862 the Eastern Bengal Railway opened a broad-gauge line from Ranaghat through Darshana to Jagati, making this the first railway station in what is now Bangladesh. The line was later pushed on to Goalundo, and Kushtia Court became the town's main station. Jagati is now out of use and in poor shape, and a plan to restore it has been waiting for approval for years. Rail lovers still come to see the old platform and building.
blocks: How to get there
From Kushtia town take an easy-bike or rickshaw to Jagati, near the sugar mill side of town.
Good to know
The building is old and neglected, so watch your step and keep off the tracks.

glance: 205 km to Kushtia by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
jhaudia-shahi-mosque.desc: The Jhaudia Shahi Mosque stands in Jhaudia village in Kushtia Sadar upazila. Its exact date is unknown; a plaque at the entrance ties it to Aurangzeb's reign, and local tradition credits a saint called Shah Sufi Adari Mia. The long, narrow prayer hall has domes on the roof and a minaret at each corner, built of brick and lime mortar in the Mughal manner. It has been on the Department of Archaeology's list since 1969, and every Friday people come from far away to pray, so a small fair gathers outside.
blocks: How to get there
From Kushtia town take an easy-bike or CNG south to Jhaudia village.
Good to know
Fridays are crowded and lively; come on another day for a quiet look. Dress modestly and ask before entering the prayer hall.

glance: 205 km to Kushtia by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
tagore-lodge-kushtia.desc: Tagore Lodge stands in the Milpara area of Kushtia town. Rabindranath Tagore had it built in 1895 to run Tagore & Company, a business he and his nephews set up after moving it from Shilaidaha to Kushtia. He is said to have written poems here that later appeared in Khanika and Katha O Kahini. Kushtia municipality restored the building and opened it as a museum in 2008, with a bust of the poet at the entrance, copies of his books and a set of paintings inside.
blocks: How to get there
It is inside Kushtia town; take a rickshaw or easy-bike to Milpara.
Good to know
Pair it with Lalon's shrine at Cheuria and the Shilaidaha Kuthibari on the same day; this is the town house, not the Shilaidaha estate.

glance: Shops around Kushtia town and Mojampur; hawkers on trains
kushtia-tiler-khaja.desc: Tiler khaja is Kushtia's signature sweet, made by pulling and folding boiled sugar into airy layers and coating it in sesame seeds. Locals say it dates back over a century, and family workshops still make it by hand. It is light, crisp and not too sweet. Packed in small boxes, it is the classic souvenir from Kushtia.

lalon-smaran-utsab.desc: Each year on 1 Kartik, mid-October, the anniversary of Lalon's death, Cheuria fills with Bauls, fakirs and music lovers from across Bengal. Groups sit under tents singing his songs through the night, alongside a large fair and formal stage programmes. A second gathering takes place at Dol Purnima in spring. It is one of the most important events in Bangladesh's folk music calendar.
blocks: Good to know
Book rooms in Kushtia early; keep valuables secure in the crowds.

glance: 205 km to Kushtia by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
mir-mosharraf-hossain-home.desc: Mir Mosharraf Hossain, whose Bishad Sindhu is a classic of Bengali prose, was born in Lahinipara near Kumarkhali in 1847. A memorial complex with a library stands at his family homestead. Few travellers stop, though it lies close to the Shilaidaha route. Nearby Kumarkhali was also home to journalist Kangal Harinath, whose old printing press is preserved.
blocks: How to get there
From Kushtia take a bus to Kumarkhali, then a rickshaw to Lahinipara.
Good to know
Opening times are informal; ask the caretaker.

kushtia-shon-papdi.desc: Shon papdi is made by pulling sugar syrup and roasted flour into fine threads, then pressing them into soft, crumbly squares. Kushtia's workshops are known for it alongside tiler khaja. It dissolves almost instantly on the tongue, with a nutty, buttery taste. Hawkers carry both sweets across the country.

glance: 205 km to Kushtia by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
Ticketed, approx.; higher rate for foreigners
shilaidaha-kuthibari.desc: Rabindranath Tagore spent long periods in the 1890s at Shilaidaha, managing the family estate and travelling the rivers by houseboat. The three-storey kuthibari with its distinctive sloping roof is now a museum of his photographs, furniture and paintings. Many of the songs and poems later collected in Gitanjali are linked to his years here. Large gardens and a pond surround the house.
blocks: How to get there
By auto or bus from Kushtia town via Kumarkhali road (about 45 min), or by boat across the Gorai.
Good to know
Usually closed on Sundays as a Department of Archaeology site; check before going. Tagore's birth anniversary in May brings cultural events.

glance: 205 km to Kushtia by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
swastipur-shahi-mosque.desc: Swastipur Shahi Mosque stands in Swastipur village of Alampur union, about 11 km from Kushtia town on the Jhenaidah road. Researchers date it to around 1660, when Shaista Khan was governor of Bengal, which makes it one of the oldest signs of Islam in the district. The prayer hall is small, with thick walls and a slightly larger central dome among smaller ones. It has been repaired many times and a veranda was added later, so much of the old fabric is hidden, but it is still in daily use.
blocks: How to get there
Take a Jhenaidah-bound bus or a CNG from Kushtia town and get off at Swastipur (about 11 km).
Good to know
A short stop on the way to or from Jhenaidah; avoid prayer times if you want to look around.

glance: 205 km to Kushtia by road, 5–7 hours by bus or car
bheramara-hardinge-bridge.desc: Opened in 1915, the Hardinge Bridge carries the railway over the Padma between Bheramara in Kushtia and Paksey in Pabna. Its long run of steel trusses was one of the great engineering works of British India. Beside it runs the newer Lalon Shah road bridge. The riverbank at Bheramara gives good views of both, especially at sunset.
blocks: How to get there
Train or bus from Kushtia to Bheramara (about 45 min), then a rickshaw to the riverbank.
Good to know
Do not walk on the railway tracks; view from the riverbank or the road bridge.
